speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did it follow any specific injury or bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Can you describe the specific mechanism of injury in more detail, such as whether the finger was hyperextended or flexed when it got caught? Also, is there any visible deformity, bruising, or instability when you try to move the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mechanism of injury combined with the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint and the finger resting in extension is highly suggestive of a specific tendon injury. To confirm if this is a mallet finger caused by extensor tendon avulsion or rupture, I need to visualize the bone and soft tissue structures.

REQUEST TEST: Right Ring Finger X-Ray

text: RESULTS: X-ray_of_the_Right_Hand: Findings: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture, which points strongly toward a pure extensor tendon injury. Can you confirm if there is any numbness or tingling in the fingertip, and does the finger remain straight even when you try to actively bend it?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the mechanism of injury, the physical exam findings of an extended DIP joint with an inability to actively flex, and the negative X-ray, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
